copy.title: Copy the address
copy.caption: In Leafen, press Copy address. This is the address {{app}} connects to.

signIn.title: Log in to Leafen
signIn.caption: If Leafen asks you to log in, enter the code from the workspace name in the sidebar → Add a device on a logged-in device.

allow.title: Allow the connection
allow.caption: Choose the workspaces {{app}} can use and press Allow connection.

open.title: Add a custom connector
open.caption: In Claude on the web or desktop, open Customize → Connectors, then + Add → Add custom connector.

address.title: Name and address
address.caption: Type a name, paste the address into MCP server URL and press Continue.

auth.title: How it logs in
auth.caption: Under Authentication keep Sign in now; under OAuth client choose Register automatically. Press Add.

connect.title: Connect
connect.caption: Leafen is in the list now. Press Connect beside it.

done.title: Connected
done.caption: Claude can use Leafen in your chats now.

mock.intro: Connect Claude to your data and tools.
mock.name: Name
mock.urlHint: The HTTPS address where the server accepts MCP requests, for example https://mcp.example.com/mcp.

open.title: Add a custom MCP server
open.caption: In ChatGPT on the web, open Plugins, press + and choose Add custom MCP server. It shows when your plan and workspace allow it.

address.title: Name and address
address.caption: Type a name, paste the address under Connection, choose OAuth, tick I understand and want to continue, then press Create as a plugin.

done.title: Use it in a chat
done.caption: Install the plugin, then type @ in a new chat and pick Leafen.

mock.name: Name
mock.understand: I understand and want to continue

claudePort: Claude’s connector can’t connect to this address on port {{port}}. The steps for adding it to Claude show at an address on port 443.
